subject: Simulation run: Indemnity notice sequencing for Brightwell order form

Subject: Request: run a notice-sequencing simulation before finalizing OF

Jordan,

Hope you’re well. Legal at Brightwell here — we’re running a short simulation internally this week to verify sequencing in the Order Form indemnity language before signature. We have a hypothetical third-party patent assertion scenario and want to walk through notice -> evidence capture -> defend/control handoff -> cost allocation to validate timelines.

Key asks from our side:
- Can Redwood run a one-hour tabletop with our counsel to step through the flow (notice, rebuttal window, evidence handoff)?
- Do you have a standard simulation runbook and a recommended notice window? Our procurement prefers 30 days but counsel is thinking 45.
- If Redwood asserts right-to-defend, can you outline the typical cooperation obligations and insurance/escrow triggers?

Attached is a quick scenario doc (brightwell-sim-scenario.pdf) with the facts we’ll use.

We’d like to schedule this week if possible — proposed times in the attachment. Thanks for moving quickly on this.

Best,
Eliot Barnes
Head of Legal, Brightwell AI
eliot.barnes@brightwell.ai

Eli —

Thanks for the scenario. We can absolutely run a tabletop and walk the parties through our defend-vs-reimburse sequencing plus ops playbooks. I’ll coordinate internal attendees (legal + CS + ops). Preliminary thoughts:
- We have a short simulation runbook we can circulate (rdw-indemnity-sim-runbook_v1.docx) that maps steps to owners and artifacts.
- For commercial cadence, 30 days is often tight for cross-border evidence collection; Kimberly, what do you think of 45 days for the notice/evidence window versus 30?
- We can map insurance offsets and escrow activation conditions during the run.

Proposed approach: we’ll run an internal Redwood-only dry run first (30–45 min) to validate the runbook and then do a joint 60 min tabletop with Brightwell counsel.

I’ll share times in a separate calendar invite — can you confirm two preferred slots from the attachment?

Best,

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Request: run a notice-sequencing simulation before finalizing OF

Jordan / team —

Quick legal take ahead of the tabletop:

1) Defense control vs. reimbursement: we typically prefer right-to-defend for third-party IP claims; where customers object, we offer a defend-with-reimbursement option with a reimbursement cap tied to fees/settlement amounts. I’d like us to prepare three options with a risk matrix (low / medium / high exposure) — I attached a draft risk matrix (rdw-risk-matrix.xlsx).

2) Notice & evidence window: 45 days gives us breathing room for triage and to collect KV cache and recall logs from infra. For international customers we also need to check cross-border evidence transfer restrictions. Recommend we propose 45 days as our default ask and note a fallback of 30 days with expedited escalation steps.

3) Cooperation mechanics: include clear timelines for initial acknowledgement, technical evidence export (who is the custodian), and a named engineer liaison. We should also define privilege preservation language for shared analysis and a template evidence checklist.

4) Canary/fallback plan: suggest adding an operational fallback clause that allows an automatic switch to a vetted model variant (lower-risk quantized model) if infringement risk is material during triage.

I can draft short redline language for the three options and circulate before the internal dry run.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Request: run a notice-sequencing simulation before finalizing OF

Team —

Short commercial note from Sales: to keep the deal momentum we should present two clean options to Brightwell during the tabletop:

A) Right-to-defend (Redwood lead). Brightwell gets cooperation commitments, damage cap negotiated separately.
B) Right-to-reimburse (customer lead) — Redwood agrees to reimburse defense costs up to an agreed cap; in exchange Brightwell accepts a modest one-time onboarding credit or a 6-month service credit if an indemnity event occurs.

If Kimberly can provide the three-option redlines by EOD today, I’ll package the two commercial compromises so procurement has a simple yes/no on the call.

—Ben
